summary: François 'Papa Doc' Duvalier, a Haitian doctor turned president for life, ruled Haiti through the Tonton Macoute terror militia from 1957 to 1971; his son Jean-Claude 'Baby Doc' looted the country with US support until fleeing in 1986.

evidence.note: Francois Duvalier's birth in 1907 amid political chaos
US Marine occupation 1915-1934 spanning Duvalier's youth, with massacres of protesters
medical career fighting yaws and malaria in the interior
black nationalist movement aimed against the mixed-race elite and US occupiers
army-backed election win in September 1957 starts the regime
creation of the Tonton Macoute militia under Clement Barbot
US military mission helps crush 1959 exile invasion to keep Duvalier in power
Barbot's insurgency against the regime and his death in 1963
Papa Doc dies in 1971 after naming his son successor
Baby Doc flees Haiti in February 1986 on a US aircraft
Baby Doc returns in 2011 and dies in 2014
long background segment on colonial slavery and the Haitian Revolution

notes: Roughly the first 50 minutes of part 1 cover Haitian history from 1492 through the revolution, the 1825 French indemnity and 19th-century instability. I treated this as background before the story begins, so covered_span starts at Papa Doc's birth (1907). Reviewers may want to extend it. Polities left empty because the colonial era is background. Roles apply mainly to Papa Doc; Baby Doc is dictator-autocrat only.
